elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: 14.2(B) retained: "M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against...", and the defined term "Customer" is Tri City National Bank "(including its Affiliates)", so the defence duty runs to affiliates; 14.3 confirms "the indemnifying party shall be obligated to defend such indemnitee".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 14.2(B) indemnifies "Customer" (defined to include its Affiliates) against "any liability or expenses arising out of or relating to (i) any claim by a third party...".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Head (i) is limited to claims that "the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark" — it omits trade-secret/misappropriation and non-US IP rights, and no Deliverables concept is covered. To meet the preferred element the head must read "any intellectual property right" (including misappropriation) without the US-only, three-right limitation.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Head (iv) covers only "a violation of Federal, state, or other laws or regulations for the protection of persons or members of a protected class" — not Vendor's breach of applicable law generally. A head reading "M&I's breach of applicable law" would be required.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No head in 14.2(B) addresses unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data; heads (vi)-(vii) reach only injury/death and tangible property or financial loss from acts or omissions. An express data-breach head is missing.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: 14.2(B) contains no gross-negligence or wilful-misconduct head; (vii) is limited to property damage or financial loss from acts or omissions and does not name gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: 14.3: "such indemnitee shall give notice of such claim to the indemnifying party, including a brief description of the amount and basis therefor".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: 14.3: indemnifying party "shall be entitled to assume control of the defense of the claim with counsel chosen by the indemnifying party, reasonably satisfactory to the indemnitee".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: 14.3: "Indemnitee shall cooperate fully with, and assist, the indemnifying party in its defense against such claim in all reasonable respects."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Paragraph 14.2(A) (Customer indemnity) is left untouched and no limiting language to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law appears anywhere in the rendered text; the drafter expressly declines to narrow it.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.2(B)(i): "M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against, any liability or expenses arising out of or relating to (i) any claim by a third party that the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark of a third party".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the condition does not apply because the indemnity carries no Customer-modification exclusion. Leaving the indemnity unqualified is more favourable to us than the fallback tolerates, so nothing was required.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination carve-out exists in 14.2(B)(i) and none was added, which is better than the fallback permits, so the element is satisfied without edit.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion is present or added, so the tolerance is unused and the element is met.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: New paragraph: "M&I shall, at its option, procure for Customer the right to continue using the Services or M&I's software, or modify or replace the infringing item so that it is non-infringing", triggered by "a claim described in Paragraph B(i)".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: New paragraph: "if none of the foregoing remedies is reasonably available, M&I shall refund to Customer the fees paid for the infringing item."

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: New paragraph: "M&I's total liability under Paragraph B shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid by Customer under this Agreement", and 13.4 now opens "Except as provided in Section 14.2(C)", so the three-month general cap no longer swallows the indemnity. The super-cap exceeds, rather than sits below, the general cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the retained 14.2(B)(i) IP indemnity with defence, plus the inserted procure/modify/replace-or-refund remedy and the 3x annual fees cap carved out of Section 13.4, meet all seven fallback elements. The three exclusion elements are permissive and are met because no Customer modification/combination/specification carve-outs exist or were added.

Preferred is not complete: no breach-of-applicable-law head (only protected-class laws), no Vendor data-breach head, no gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct head, IP head limited to United States patent, copyright and trademark (no misappropriation/trade secret, no non-US rights, no Deliverables), and Customer's indemnity in 14.2(A) is not narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to a concise remedies-plus-super-cap insertion and a single conforming carve-out phrase in 13.4. No survival tail, expense, fee-shifting or damages extras were added, and the existing unqualified indemnity heads are preserved.

Drafting repair (not element-fatal): the inserted paragraph is rendered without its "C." designation while 13.4 cross-refers to "Section 14.2(C)". Label the new paragraph "C." within Section 14.2 so the cross-reference is not left dangling.

Tightening suggestion: the substitution deleted 13.4's lead-in "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement" entirely; the narrower formulation "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement other than Section 14.2(C)" would achieve the same carve-out while leaving the rest of that sentence's priority language untouched.

Note for negotiation, not a defect: the super-cap is expressed on "Paragraph B" as a whole, which usefully lifts every Vendor indemnity head out of the three-month cap; confirm we are content that it also functions as a ceiling on the non-IP heads (previously capped far lower).
